To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exercise training induces a nonuniform adaptation of control of coronary vascular tone that is spatially distributed in the coronary arterial bed.

exercise training alters control of coronary vascular function by altering endothelial function, vascular smooth muscle function, and myogenic reactivity in a spatially and temporally distributed manner throughout the coronary arterial bed.

exercise training induced adaptive changes in the coronary circulation are nonuniform throughout the coronary arterial bed and that exercise training induced changes in the coronary vasculature are mediated in part through altered control of coronary blood flow by endothelial and vascular muscle cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exercise training on coronary vascular control and the cellular mechanisms involved in these effects.
the effects of exercise training on the regulation of the coronary circulation and the cellular mechanisms involved in these adaptations.
the mechanisms by which exercise training alters coronary vascular function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

exercise training alters the control of coronary vascular tone and that these changes in control are spatially distributed throughout the coronary tree and are likely to be different in large and small coronary arteries.
exercise training induces adaptations in control of coronary blood flow throughout the coronary arterial system, and the nature of these adaptations varies throughout the coronary tree.

exercise training induces an increased coronary blood flow capacity in large and small coronary arteries and that the adaptive mechanisms that contribute to this increased blood flow capacity are complex and nonuniform in their spatial distribution throughout the coronary arterial system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

exercise training alters endothelium mediated and vascular smooth muscle mediated control systems in the microcirculatory and large coronary arterial beds and that the magnitude and direction of these changes vary with the level in the coronary vascular tree and the mode, frequency and duration of exercise training.

exercise training induces adaptations in the coronary vascular control system that are distributed throughout the coronary arterial system, that the mode and intensity of exercise may influence the adaptive responses, that endothelial and vascular myogenic mechanisms play important roles, and that there is a spatial distribution of these adaptations in the coronary tree.
exercise training induces a nonuniform distribution of adaptations in the coronary vasculature and that these adaptations are associated with changes in endothelial and vascular myocyte phenotypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

exercise training induces adaptations in the coronary vascular bed that are spatially and functionally nonuniform, and these training induced adaptations in control of coronary vasomotor tone may be different in conduit coronary arteries than in small resistance arteries.

the coronary circulation is a complex system that is regulated by multiple control systems, and exercise training induces adaptations that vary in their magnitude and in the degree to which they contribute to control of coronary blood flow.
exercise training induced changes in endothelial and smooth muscle function in the coronary arterial circulation are complex, and the mechanisms underlying these changes are not fully understood.
